Run it on your own plugin
Adjusting a verdict by what the plugin did on this machine

plugin-qualify

Can this audio plugin be hosted in a real-time audio engine, and at what cost? plugin-qualify scans a plugin, measures it offline (latency and CPU cost per rate and quantum), runs it under a real host (mod-host, with an AddressSanitizer build), and gives one verdict. Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later (LICENSE).

Install

plugin-qualify is published, signed, in the OpenMixer package channel, for Fedora 44 (x86_64, aarch64) and for Debian bookworm and trixie, including Raspberry Pi OS (amd64, arm64).

Fedora:

sudo dnf install https://www.openmixer.org/rpm/openmixer-release.noarch.rpm
sudo dnf install plugin-qualify

Debian and Raspberry Pi OS:

curl -fsSLO https://www.openmixer.org/deb/openmixer-release.deb && sudo apt install ./openmixer-release.deb
sudo apt update
sudo apt install plugin-qualify

From the npm registry:

pnpm add @openmixer/plugin-qualify
# or, to install the command globally:
npm install -g @openmixer/plugin-qualify

The npm package ships the TypeScript command only, not the native tools. The CLAP prober, the LV2 measurer and the interposer come with the RPM or DEB, or from make -C native in a checkout; with the npm package alone, point OMX_CLAP_QUALIFY, OMX_LV2_MEASURE and OMX_RT_INTERPOSE at them (the probe runner is plugin-hostd's, OMX_PROBE_RUNNER), or CLAP qualification and the LV2 hosting dimensions refuse with "no CLAP prober at ...".

The GitHub release also carries the packed tarball, openmixer-plugin-qualify-<version>.tgz. To run from a checkout instead (Node.js 20 or newer and pnpm 10, see BUILDING.md):

git clone https://github.com/FreeMixer/plugin-qualify.git
cd plugin-qualify
pnpm install
pnpm exec plugin-qualify --help

It needs Node.js 18 or newer to run. The measuring tools also want Python 3 with the lilv bindings (python3-lilv) and, for the hosting sweep, mod-host. The Containerfile builds an image with all of them. The commands below are written as plugin-qualify; from a checkout run them with pnpm exec.

Run it on your own plugin

plugin-qualify urn:example:my-plugin          # one plugin, by URI
plugin-qualify ./my-plugin.lv2                # every plugin in a bundle
plugin-qualify --all --out ./qualification   # every LV2 bundle on LV2_PATH and every CLAP on the search path, one record each
plugin-qualify --help                         # every option and its default

--format json prints the verdicts as JSON; --out <dir> writes the full measurement document. --isolate measures each plugin in a fresh worker so a crash or hang takes only that plugin. The Containerfile builds an image with lilv, mod-host and the ASan mod-host, if you do not want to install them yourself.

A named LV2 plugin is measured the same way as a CLAP one: through the probe runner, then judged from the probe output it writes (plugin-qualify judge below). Exit code: 0 every plugin qualified, 1 some did not, 2 something could not be measured.

The measurement grid

A plugin is measured in cells, each one sample rate and one quantum (block size in frames). The verdict a host gets reads the cell of that host's rate and quantum, so the grid has to hold it.

plugin-qualify --all --out ./q                          # the full grid (the default): 4 rates x 4 block sizes
plugin-qualify --all --grid-hosts --out ./q             # the hosts' grid, the fast option (also --grid hosts)
plugin-qualify --grid 48000/128,96000/1024 urn:my:fx    # exactly these cells
  • --grid hosts (the fast option; --grid-hosts says the same): the rate and quantum of every host the run judges (each --host-profile, and the console's two tiers, openmixer-console and the format's isolated host), then quantum 512 at every --rates rate, so that a record stays comparable with the ones written before the grid. With the four shipped hosts that is seven cells: 96000/1024 (openmixer-console), 48000/256 (jalv), 48000/128 (mod-host, omx-clap-host), and 512 at 44100, 48000, 96000 and 192000.
  • --grid full (the default; every plugin is measured under the same conditions, so any host's verdict can be read at any cell and the figures compare): every --rates rate at every --quanta quantum, 16 cells with the defaults (44100, 48000, 96000, 192000 by 128, 256, 512, 1024).
  • --grid <rate>/<quantum>,...: exactly the cells named.

The cells are taken in that order: the hosts' own cells first, in the order the hosts are named, then the 512 cells, then the rest by rate and quantum. --cells-per-plugin-budget N keeps the first N, so a first pass over a large machine can measure the hosts' cells alone (--cells-per-plugin-budget 3 with the four shipped hosts). --blocks N shortens the CLAP sweep of each cell from 512 blocks to N; the LV2 pass has a fixed shape (30 lifecycles and 3 swept runs per cell) and is not shortened by it.

An LV2 plugin is measured on the same grid as a CLAP one. plugin-hostd's runner measures an LV2 plugin at one rate per run (the highest it is given), which is why records written before the grid hold LV2 figures at 192000 only; plugin-qualify now runs it once per cell. A CLAP plugin is run once per quantum, at every rate of the grid at that quantum. The runs of one plugin and one offer make one probe output: the grid points of every run, the steps of every run, and the run's outcome. The record and its byte copy hold that document.

A run that ended badly leaves a grid point at each of its cells with the run's outcome in place of figures, so a cell is never silently absent. The cost a host is judged by is read at its cell: a measured cell is compared with the host's budget; a cell whose run failed reads unknown with that run's outcome (probe.oom, say); only a cell the grid does not hold reads hosting.cost.unmeasured-at-rate-and-quantum.

The memory bound

A sampler loading its library can take all the memory of a small machine, and the kernel then kills it, or something else. Every run is bounded: --memory-limit <bytes> (512M, 2G, or off), by default half of the machine's RAM. The bound is the runner's data limit (--data-bytes, RLIMIT_DATA on the measuring child: its heap and private writable mappings), and the interposer the child runs under turns an allocation refused under that limit into an immediate exit with status 121. A run that ends that way, or by a SIGKILL the runner did not send (the kernel's out-of-memory killer), is recorded as probe.oom: its cells carry the outcome and memoryLimit { bytes, mechanism }, the plugin's record is still written, and the other cells are judged as usual. A plugin whose every run ended probe.oom is unknown under every host, deciding probe.oom. A host whose own cell ended probe.oom is unknown there as well (memory, probe.oom): the plugin did not run within the bound at that host's rate and quantum.

Where the machine delegates the memory controller, the runner sets the bound as memory.max of a cgroup instead: a run the kernel kills at it is probe.memory-limit, read the same way, and the document's limits says which it was. A process plugin-qualify spawns itself, with no runner (tools/lv2-measure.mjs, tools/benchmark.py), runs under RLIMIT_AS at the machine's RAM, off for a sanitizer build; hitting it is memory-limit-exceeded, with the limit.

Memory

Each cell carries a footprint: how far the resident set of a process of its own grew, in KB, after instantiate, after activate, at rest after processing, with notes held for an instrument, and what a second instance added. A record adds what they come to: firstInstanceKb, the most one instance held with everything its instances share, and perInstanceKb, what one more costs.

A host with a memory budget reads them, at every cell it runs, and the verdict follows: hosting.memory.within-ceiling, hosting.memory.above-ceiling (unsuitable), or hosting.memory.unmeasured (unknown, since a missing figure never reads as fitting). openmixer-console has one, sized for the desk, and the Raspberry Pi hosts openmixer-pi-4gb and openmixer-pi-8gb, at 48000/128 and 48000/256, have one each. The Pi budgets are not measured on a Pi yet, so a plugin under them is conditional, hosting.memory.within-provisional-ceiling: that gives the figure and the ceiling and does not say the plugin fits. The other hosts have no budget, and read nothing.

A soak (LV2; the CLAP prober has no continuous render yet) also reads the growth: past 10 MB per minute of audio over its second half, provisional, the rate fails as leaks.

How long a run takes

The default grid is the full one, so the expected time of a run with no grid option is the full row: about 65 hours on a Raspberry Pi 5 for the vangelis set (1823 records). --grid-hosts is the fast option, about 30 hours there.

Times from one deep run on a Raspberry Pi 5 (4 cores, 4 GB), 1823 records (494 CLAP, two offers of each of 247, and 1329 LV2), six hours in all with the grid of before (CLAP at four rates in one run at quantum 512, LV2 at 192000/512 alone):

runs mean a run total
CLAP, one run per offer (4 cells) 494 2.8 s 0.38 h
LV2, one run (1 cell) 1329 10.5 s 3.86 h
host admissions (jalv, mod-host) and the scan about 1.8 h

A CLAP plugin takes one run per quantum of the grid, an LV2 plugin one run per cell; the admissions do not grow with the grid. On that machine, then, about:

grid CLAP runs a plugin LV2 runs a plugin expected
hosts (7 cells) 4 7 1.5 h + 27 h + 1.8 h, about 30 h
full (16 cells) 4 16 1.5 h + 62 h + 1.8 h, about 65 h
hosts, --cells-per-plugin-budget 3 3 3 1.1 h + 11.6 h + 1.8 h, about 15 h

These are ceilings: the LV2 time a run was taken at 192000, the dearest rate. --blocks 128 takes a quarter of the CLAP sweep a cell. A first pass with --cells-per-plugin-budget 3, then --grid full over the plugins worth it, keeps a small machine's night bounded.

CLAP plugins: the RT-safety verdict

A .clap file, or a directory holding one, is scanned by omx-clap-scan (from omx-clap-core; set OMX_CLAP_SCAN to its path when it is not on PATH) and each plugin in it is then qualified by the CLAP prober the package installs (from a checkout, the one built from native/, see BUILDING.md):

plugin-qualify ./my-fx.clap                   # every plugin in the file
plugin-qualify --out ./out ./my-fx.clap       # and its RT-safety documents
CLAP_PATH=~/my-clap plugin-qualify --all      # every CLAP on the search path

Each plugin is measured by plugin-hostd's probe runner, plugin-hostd-probe (from the plugin-hostd package, 0.4.0 or later, which the RPM and DEB require; OMX_PROBE_RUNNER names it when it is not on PATH). The runner starts the prober under limits (a wall clock that kills the whole process tree, CPU time, memory, files), and plugin-qualify waits for the runner and reads the document it writes, the probe output. Nothing in plugin-qualify times a prober out on its own any more.

The files a pin holds are plugin-hostd's: the sync writes each pin with the files plugin-hostd --pin-files <uri> prints for the device's LV2 directories (plugin-hostd 0.15.0 or later; PLUGIN_HOSTD names the daemon when it is not on PATH), the list an add checks, and hashes exactly those. When plugin-hostd cannot name them, or is older, the plugin gets no pin, the log says why, and the daemon pins it on its first add (pin_mode first-use).

--all walks the standard CLAP search path through the same scanner: each directory CLAP_PATH names (colon-separated), then ~/.clap, then /usr/lib/clap, which is the system directory on every distribution and architecture. A plugin id found twice keeps its first place on that path. LV2 plugins are measured by tools/lv2-measure.mjs (below); this entry point does not drive that pass yet, so --all refuses with exit 2 when any .lv2 bundle is on the LV2 path (LV2_PATH, else ~/.lv2 and the system lv2 directories) rather than qualify only the CLAP side. A directory on the CLAP path that cannot be read (permissions, a symlink loop) also refuses with exit 2, naming it.

The prober runs each plugin headless at every cell of the grid (see "The measurement grid"), under an interposer that counts the allocations, locks and syscalls its process() makes while every parameter is swept, and prints the file's SHA-256 beside what it measured. The verdict is the real-time-safety one: suitable only on a clean count, conditional (isolated in the pin: it runs in a worker of its own, never refused) on any allocation, lock, syscall or main-thread host call from process(), unsuitable on CLAP_PROCESS_ERROR, unknown when it could not be counted. An instrument is quiet until it is played, so a plugin with a note input is also played, at every rate and under a count of its own: a chord, the pitch bent and a controller moved, pressure, the chord let go, a burst of 32 note ons in one block and their offs, all notes off, in the dialect its note input reads (CLAP's, else MIDI's). An allocation, lock or syscall while it plays is conditional, isolated in the pin like the same violation in the run (hosting.rt-safety.violations-under-notes); an instrument that could not be played under the interposer is unknown (hosting.rt-safety.notes-unmeasured). --out writes the qualification records and the probe outputs they judged (see "Judging a probe output" below), one pair per plugin binary and offered host extensions. Each plugin's pin is an integrity block in the probe output: the .clap's SHA-256 by its file name and the parameter-layout fingerprint omx-layout/1:<sha256>, both computed through plugin-hostd's pin.h, which is what a console hands plugin-hostd as pin_set before it adds the plugin. OMX_CLAP_QUALIFY and OMX_RT_INTERPOSE name the prober and the interposer the runner starts when they are not the installed ones or the checkout's own build.

Judging a probe output

The probe output is the document plugin-hostd-probe run writes: one binary and one offer, the steps the prober reached and how each ended, and the figures per rate and quantum, with no verdict in it. plugin-qualify reads it with readProbeOutput, which refuses a document of a major version it does not know (probe.format.major-unknown), a document that carries a verdict, and a document whose derived fields disagree with the fields they are computed from (probe.format.derived-mismatch): machine.class.cstatesLimited and machine.profile.meetsProtocol are recomputed from cpuidle[], the governor and unmet[], never trusted.

plugin-hostd-probe run --out out/plate.probe.json ./example-plate.clap org.example.plate
plugin-qualify judge --host-profile omx-clap-host --qualification-dir ./qualification out/plate.probe.json

judge writes, into the qualification directory (--qualification-dir, else $XDG_STATE_HOME/omx/qualification, else ~/.local/state/omx/qualification), the qualification record <id>@<version>-<sha256 first 12>.<offer>.qualification.json and, beside it, a byte copy of the probe output it judged, <same name>.probe.json, because the probe directory may be wiped. The record names that copy and its SHA-256 in probe, with the run's protocol, reason and machine class, so a reference figure and a local one are told apart. The record holds, for each host profile, the verdict (rating, hosting, the deciding reason code and every reason) and the cost reasons at that profile's rate and quantum, and the figures as measured. Exit 0 every plugin qualified, 1 some did not, 2 something could not be read or judged.

The verdict is the same one plugin-qualify gives CLAP plugins, the real-time-safety one, now for LV2 as well; cost is reported beside it, not folded into it. Cost is read at the profile's rate AND quantum: a pair the document does not hold reads hosting.cost.unmeasured-at-rate-and-quantum, and two quanta of one plugin that cost differently give two different cost reasons. Only a measurement of the old format, which keeps one figure per rate, is read per rate. A run that did not end probe.ok is unknown, with the run's outcome code as the reason.

An instrument costs nothing until a voice plays, so its cost is taken with notes held down, at velocity 127, spread across the keyboard, while every parameter is swept: as many notes as the voice capacity the plugin declares (CLAP voice-info, basis declared), or, when it declares none, the count --probe-notes gives (basis probe; LV2 declares none). Each rate's figure says how many notes it held and why (voices: { held, basis, capacity }). An instrument with no count to hold is not timed (voices-unknown).

An LV2 plugin's record holds the same two figures, under the same field names, in measurements.grid[]: latency { declaredFrames, measuredFrames } and cost. lv2_measure takes them at the run's rate and block, the way the CLAP prober does: the declared figure is what the plugin reports on its latency port (lv2:designation lv2:latency, or the older lv2:reportsLatency; 0 when it has none), the measured one is where an impulse at frame 0 lands (the first frame at or above 1e-3 of the response's own peak), or, for an instrument, where a struck A4 sounds. A plugin that has no latency port is measured, never read as 0. An instrument's cost holds OMX_PROBE_NOTES keys down (the LV2 counterpart of --probe-notes). A figure the run could not take (a response that stays silent, an instrument with no count to hold) is left out of the grid point and named in measurements.unmeasured with its hosting code (hosting.latency.unmeasured, hosting.cost.unmeasured-at-rate-and-quantum).

Every cell of a record carries latency: the two figures when the run took them, else { unmeasuredReason, code }, the contract's word for why and the hosting code a reader classifies by. A latency step that did not end well gives the child's reason (silent-output, say); a cell whose run failed, its outcome's word (probe-crashed, or probe-error for probe.oom); a run that took no latency at all (a runner or a child older than the latency arm), not-attempted. The declared figure alone, for a plugin whose response could not be measured, is not in the probe output: plugin-hostd's runner writes a cell's latency only with both figures.

The prober also scans: OMX_CLAP_SCAN=native/build/clap-qualify makes it the scanner, and its scan keeps what a console needs to draw a third-party plugin's controls: an enum parameter's labels (as the plugin's value_to_text renders them), each parameter's module, and the plugin's remote-control pages.

Adjusting a verdict by what the plugin did on this machine

plugin-qualify adjust --history ~/.local/state/plugin-hostd/history --qualification-dir ./qualification --host-profile omx-clap-host
plugin-qualify adjust --history history --qualification-dir ./qualification --host-class aarch64/4/2400 --pins pins.txt

plugin-hostd keeps a running history of every plugin binary on every host class it ran on (windows run alone and in a group, CPU, xrun windows, crashes, restarts, quarantines). adjust reads that file directly, so it runs without a daemon, and writes a second verdict beside the measured one in each qualification record: a history block per host class of the file, holding the line it looked for (the plugin's plugin-hostd uri and the digest of the first file of its pin), whether the history has it, the windows it counts, and for each --host-profile the measured pin verdict, the adjusted one, the move (demote, promote or none) and a reason code. The measured verdicts and the measurement are never changed: the same plugin on another host class has another history and another adjusted verdict.

move when reason
in-process to isolated a crash was counted within 30 days, on this host class history.crashed
in-process to isolated from 30 grouped windows, the share of xrun windows grouped exceeds the share alone by 5 points history.xruns-grouped
isolated to refused three or more solo crashes, the latest within 30 days history.crashed-alone
isolated to in-process every reason against the plugin is a hosting.cost.* one, 360 windows run alone (six hours), no crash or restart ever counted, no xruns raised when grouped, cpu_p95_solo under the host profile's ceiling history.steady
none no line for this binary on this class history.no-record
none a line, and no rule moves the verdict history.no-change
none the line would promote, but the verdict is a fact about the plugin: a real-time-safety, feature, stability, latency or topology reason, an unknown, or a refused history.not-liftable, with blockedBy

History never lifts a real-time-safety, feature or unknown verdict, and never promotes a refused one; a demotion is one step. The thresholds are one table, HISTORY_POLICY in src/history-adjust.ts. --pins <file> writes the pins with the adjusted verdict of the first --host-profile instead of the measured one; it needs exactly one host class, so name one with --host-class when the history holds several. --now <seconds> fixes the time the history is read at. A line of the history outside its grammar is not read and is named on stderr; a history of a version this tool does not know is refused.

LV2 plugins: the hosting measurement

tools/lv2-measure.mjs measures the hosting dimensions (stability, rtSafety, features) through the LV2 measurer the package installs, lv2_measure: each plugin is loaded through lilv in its own process, instantiated and destroyed 30 times, and run under the interposer while every control is swept. tools/lv2-measure.mjs measures at the highest --rates rate; plugin-qualify runs the measurer once per cell of its grid (see "The measurement grid"):

node tools/lv2-measure.mjs --rates 48000 --dimensions stability,rtSafety,features \
  --plugins urn:my:plugin --out measurements.json --run

Without --plugins it measures every plugin the scan finds. Each plugin's entry carries its pin, an integrity block: the SHA-256 of the files the host loads and the parameter-layout fingerprint, through plugin-hostd's pin.h, as for CLAP. OMX_LV2_MEASURE and OMX_RT_INTERPOSE name the measurer and the interposer when they are not the installed ones or the checkout's own build.

The features the measurer offers a plugin are the console's own: omx-clap-core's LV2 feature provider, the code its LV2 host builds every instance's features with. Each of the provider's options is a flag of tools/lv2-measure.mjs and of lv2_measure itself, and each plugin's record names the options it ran under, featureOptions:

flag what it sets default
--features LIST the kinds offered: map, unmap, options, bounded, worker, default-state, log, rtmempool (empty: none) all but default-state
--strict / --no-strict refuse a plugin requiring a feature not offered (the record's refusedFeature names it), or hand it to its own instantiate without it --no-strict
--block-declares LIST the buf-size declarations made when bounded is offered: bounded, fixed, pow2 (empty: none) bounded
--block-min N bufsz:minBlockLength; 0 is the run's block 1
--block-max N bufsz:maxBlockLength; 0 is the run's block 0
--block-nominal N bufsz:nominalBlockLength; 0 is the maximum 0
--log MODE log:log lines: silent, route (to stderr) or capture (into the record's featureOptions.log.lines) silent
--log-capture-bytes N the capture buffer, its NUL included 4096

The defaults are the measurement as it has always been, so a verdict reached under them does not move. lv2_measure --help lists the same flags.

Scanned descriptors

Both scanners also write what each plugin states about itself as a scanned descriptor: one JSON file per plugin in omx-contract's descriptor words (identity, controls, ports, what it needs from a host, whether it reports latency), held to omx-contract's descriptor schema before it is written. A descriptor holds no measurement and no verdict; those are the qualification record's.

The files go into the descriptor directory, the key descriptor_dir:

where
named --descriptor-dir <dir>
a user (the default) $XDG_STATE_HOME/omx/descriptors, else ~/.local/state/omx/descriptors
a system service /var/lib/omx/descriptors (--system)

Each file is named <id>@<version>-<sha256 first 12>.json: the CLAP id or the LV2 URI, the version the plugin states (unversioned when it states none) and the SHA-256 of its binary (the .clap, or the LV2 bundle's lv2:binary), with every character other than letters, digits, ., _ and - written _. The hash keys which file describes which binary: a changed binary is a new file, and the old one stays as history.

tools/scan.py --out catalog.json                                     # LV2: the catalog, and the descriptors beside it
tools/scan.py --descriptor-dir ./descriptors urn:my:plugin           # one plugin, into a directory of your own
native/build/clap-qualify --json ./my-fx.clap | tools/descriptors.py clap --descriptor-dir ./descriptors

scan.py --no-descriptors writes the catalog only. A descriptor the schema refuses is not written and is reported as contract.file.invalid, omx-contract's code; a plugin whose binary cannot be read is qualify.descriptor.binary-unhashed; a directory that cannot be written is qualify.descriptor.dir-unwritable; no schema found is qualify.descriptor.schema-missing. Any of them makes the run exit 2, and the other plugins are still written. The schema is the omx-contract package plugin-qualify depends on, else /usr/share/omx-contract/omx-contract.schema.json; OMX_CONTRACT_SCHEMA names another one, for a test. The writer needs Python's jsonschema (python3-jsonschema).

What the verdicts mean

  • suitable: every dimension was measured and passed. Safe to run inside the engine's own process. This is the only verdict that counts as qualified.
  • conditional: it works, with a caution (for example a high cost at small quanta, or an allocation, lock or syscall in run()). It is run isolated, and the deciding reason names the caution.
  • unknown: something was not measured. An unmeasured plugin is never a pass.
  • unsuitable: a measured failure: a crash, a memory error in the plugin's own binary, or a required feature the host does not provide. An allocation, lock or syscall in run() is not one: that plugin is conditional, and runs isolated.

The worst dimension decides. The text output prints the plugin, its verdict and the reason that decided it.

Reproducing a failure

  1. Run the plugin alone: plugin-qualify --format json --out ./out <uri>.
  2. The document in ./out names the dimension that failed and, for a crash, the sanitizer class and the object of the faulting frame.
  3. Run the ASan mod-host (mod-host-asan in the image) with just that plugin to get the full sanitizer report.

fixtures/zero-path.lv2 is a known-bad plugin (a zero-size atom:Path overread). It should rate unsuitable; if it does not, the sweep is not catching memory errors.

For other projects (zynthian, MOD, packagers)

The measurements describe the plugin and never the host: latency and cost per rate, whether it survives a thousand lifecycles and a three-hour soak, whether run() allocates, locks or makes syscalls, and which LV2 features it requires. They are taken once. The verdict is a separate step: the same measurements judged against a host profile, the facts that differ between hosts. Two projects share the measurements and differ only in the profile they choose.

Choosing a host profile

plugin-qualify --host-profile jalv ./my-synth.lv2                  # zynthian: one jalv process per plugin
plugin-qualify --host-profile mod-host ./my-fx.lv2                 # MOD: one shared mod-host process
plugin-qualify --host-profile omx-clap-host ./my-synth.clap        # omx-clap-host, alone or under plugin-hostd
plugin-qualify --host-profile jalv,mod-host,openmixer-console <uri>  # one verdict per profile
plugin-qualify --host-profile ./my-host.json <uri>                 # your own host
profile isolation verdict instruments LV2 features read from cost budget (P95 of a core, rate / quantum)
openmixer-console (default) in-process (the console's RT thread) judged from a declaration no the console's in-process table 0.05 at 96000 / 1024
jalv per-process measured by a run (jalv -n <name> <uri>, headless) yes jalv 1.6.8 src/jalv.c (zynthian's fork passes the same list) 0.25 at 48000 / 256
mod-host shared-process measured by a run (add, activate, remove on mod-host's socket) yes mod-host f14a230 src/effects.c 0.05 at 48000 / 128
omx-clap-host shared-process judged from a declaration yes the console's in-process table (the same LV2 feature provider) 0.05 at 48000 / 128

Measured or declared. A declared verdict is what the profile's feature list and cost budget make of the one probe output. A measured verdict (jalv, mod-host, LV2 plugins) also runs the plugin under that host, one admission per plugin, and its record entry carries arm: "run" and measured: true. A refusal (resp -102), a crash (the signal), a host that dies on add, or a port type the host does not know makes the plugin unsuitable for that host, with the code as the deciding reason (mod-host.resp-102, mod-host.signal-SIGABRT, mod-host.died-on-add, jalv.unknown-port-type, jalv.signal-SIGABRT). A host that is not installed leaves the verdict unmeasured (unknown, deciding <host>.not-installed). After any death on mod-host the next admission starts a fresh host. plugin-qualify judge reads a probe output that holds no run, so its jalv and mod-host entries stay arm: "declaration".

The console's two tiers. Every record carries tiers: the in-process verdict (openmixer-console) and the isolated verdict (omx-clap-host, an LV2 plugin through plugin-hostd's LV2 adapter), offeredOn (in-process when its verdict qualified, isolated when its verdict qualified or is conditional) and, when neither, dimmed with the reason. A conditional plugin, RT-unsafe for instance, is offered on the isolated tier with runsAlone: true: it runs in a worker of its own, never grouped, and its pin says isolated. An LV2 plugin is run once under the adapter, and that run decides its omx-clap-host verdict as a mod-host run decides mod-host's. An lv2:InstrumentPlugin is also played one held note there, its output read at its JACK ports (jack_peak): at or under -120 dBFS it reads unknown (omx-clap-host.silent-under-note), not qualified and not refused, since a sampler with nothing loaded is silent too. A level that could not be read reads the same way (omx-clap-host.level-unmeasured). A plugin that kills the isolated host and qualifies in-process is offered in-process only. The tiers are judged for every plugin whether or not --host-profile names them; mod-host and jalv are run only when --host-profile asks for them.

omx-clap-host offers a CLAP plugin the console's six host extensions and three more, clap.preset-load/2, clap.track-info/1 and clap.remote-controls/2. A CLAP plugin judged under it is probed again with those three offered, so its verdict holds for the host it runs in.

The jalv, mod-host and omx-clap-host budgets are defaults, not a measurement of your board. State your own by writing a profile file. Every field is required; a missing or mistyped field is refused and never filled in with a default:

{
  "id": "zynthian-v5",
  "lv2Features": ["http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/urid#map", "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/urid#unmap",
                  "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/worker#schedule", "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/log#log",
                  "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/options#options",
                  "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/state#loadDefaultState",
                  "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/buf-size#powerOf2BlockLength",
                  "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/buf-size#fixedBlockLength",
                  "http://lv2plug.in/ns/ext/buf-size#boundedBlockLength"],
  "clapExtensions": null,
  "instruments": true,
  "cost": { "coreFractionCeiling": 0.3, "rate": 48000, "quantum": 256 },
  "latency": "uncompensated",
  "isolation": "per-process"
}

What each field changes. lv2Features is what the host passes to instantiate: a plugin that requires anything else is unsuitable on that host. clapExtensions is null for a host with no CLAP path. instruments: true means a MIDI input is fed, and a plugin with no audio input but a MIDI input and an audio output rates as an instrument. cost is the per-instance ceiling, and the rate and quantum the verdict is judged at. latency: "compensated" means the host aligns on the plugin's latency, so a latency that moves with a control is a caution. isolation decides whether spawned threads and a linked GUI toolkit count as cautions: they do only when the plugin shares its process. An unmeasured dimension is unknown on every host.

With several profiles, the exit code is 0 only if every plugin qualifies under every profile.

The JSON document

--out <dir> writes one interchange document per run (lv2-plugin-measurements, format 1.6, the same format the OpenMixer console reads). The plugins array holds the raw, host-free measurements. Beside it, hostProfiles holds each profile the run judged against, in full, and verdicts holds one entry per plugin per profile:

{ "uri": "urn:example:verb", "host": "jalv", "rating": "unknown", "qualified": false,
  "deciding": "hosting.stability.unsoaked" }

host is the id of an entry in hostProfiles. deciding is a stable code, absent when the plugin is suitable. If you have your own host rules, re-derive them from plugins and do not trust another host's verdict.

As a library

classifyPluginHosting(plugin, { rate, quantum, profile }) gives one verdict, and qualifyPlugins(measured, { profiles }) gives one per plugin per profile. readHostProfile(json) validates a profile file, and judgedDocument(run, plugins, profiles, verdicts) builds the document. All of them are exported from the package root. The package depends on no other OpenMixer package.

Pinning what was qualified

plugin-qualify --pins pins.txt ./my-synth.clap     # a pin and a verdict per plugin, in a file plugin-hostd loads

--pins <file> writes one line per qualified plugin, the same line as plugin-hostd's pin_set verb with the verdict as a last word: the SHA-256 of every file the host loads, the parameter-layout fingerprint, and verdict=in-process (suitable), isolated (conditional) or refused (unsuitable). A plugin with no verdict is pinned without one. Put the file in plugin-hostd's settings as pin_file and an add of that plugin needs no pin_set; a changed file is refused with -509. The verdict is the first --host-profile's. A run that took no pin leaves an existing file alone.

Qualifying every plugin on a machine

plugin-qualify-sync qualifies every plugin installed on the machine, and again each one whose files change. With its pin file in plugin-hostd's settings, the daemon runs in its default mode (require_pins 1) and chains any plugin that qualified, the image's own and any installed later:

pin_file /var/lib/omx/qualified.pins          # in plugin-hostd.conf

The package ships it as a service that runs two minutes after boot and whenever a plugin directory changes, once the directory has been quiet for a minute. A run finds every .clap under the CLAP directories and every plugin of every bundle under the LV2 ones, and hashes each one's files as plugin-hostd does for a pin. A plugin whose files hash as recorded is skipped. A new or changed one gets the quick qualification through the probe runner, on the grid grid names (see "The measurement grid"): its pin, the RT-safety sweep, cost and latency, its qualification record and its descriptor. The soak is not part of it, and every record it writes says so in notMeasured (hosting.stability.unsoaked).

Each run of the runner (one cell of an LV2 plugin, one quantum of a CLAP one) has budget_s seconds, under memory_limit. One that crashes or hangs is recorded as crashed or hung, one that fails the sweep is pinned verdict=refused, and the run goes on to the next. The pin file and the state are written whole after every plugin, so a run cut short keeps what it finished. The last line counts the run:

qualified 2, skipped 0, refused 0, crashed 1, hung 1, unmeasured 0, distributed 0, 4.6 s

A plugin that is no longer found, or whose bytes changed, leaves nothing behind: its pin, its qualification record (with the probe output copied beside it) and its descriptor are removed. Records the sync did not write stay, and nothing is removed in a run that could not read a bundle, so a half-written install is no uninstall. A run looks only where its settings point: a plugin outside every directory of its format that the run scans is kept as it is (a run scoped to LV2 keeps every CLAP pin), and only one missing from a directory it scans is gone. A running plugin-hostd is told with pin_clear.

When plugin-hostd answers on hostd_port, the changed pins are also sent to it with pin_set and apply at once. plugin-hostd serves one controller at a time, so while one is connected the run says so and the pins apply at the daemon's next start.

The settings are /etc/omx/qualify.conf, one key value per line, and each is also a flag (--budget-s 30):

key default
lv2_path $LV2_PATH, else plugin-hostd's: /usr/lib64/lv2:/usr/lib/lv2:/usr/local/lib/lv2
lv2_extra /zynthian/zynthian-plugins/lv2:/zynthian/zynthian-my-data/plugins/lv2
clap_path, clap_extra $CLAP_PATH, then ~/.clap, then /usr/lib/clap; none
pin_file /var/lib/omx/qualified.pins
qualification_dir, descriptor_dir /var/lib/omx/qualification, /var/lib/omx/descriptors
state_file /var/lib/omx/qualify-sync.json
budget_s 60
host_profile omx-clap-host
grid full: every rate at every block size, 16 cells (hosts, or --grid-hosts: the cells of host_profile and of the console's two tiers, then 512 at every rate; or <rate>/<quantum>,...)
cells_per_plugin_budget 0, every cell of the grid
memory_limit half of the machine's RAM (off for none)
memory_notes 16: the notes an instrument with no declared capacity holds in a --memory-only run
hostd_port, hostd_feedback_port 5555, the next port
host_class the board's own, from the device tree (rpi5); none elsewhere
distributed_dir /usr/share/omx/qualification

Those are the service's (--system); run by a user, the files go under $XDG_STATE_HOME/omx. An LV2 directory added here belongs in plugin-hostd's lv2_path too, or the daemon cannot find the bundle it pinned. --force qualifies everything again, and --no-distributed reads no distributed record. A second plugin-qualify-sync waits for the run in progress (a lock on <state_file>.lock); --no-wait exits 0 at once and leaves a marker, and the holder runs once more at its end over what changed meanwhile.

Every run starts by bringing each pin's files up to the ones plugin-hostd --pin-files names, measuring nothing: a pin written before 0.17.3 lacks the preset files an LV2's manifest names, which plugin-hostd 0.15.0 also checks, and its add answers -509 until then. The new list replaces the old one when no file both lists hold changed its hash, so the verdict stands; a changed file is measured again by the run. --refresh-pins does only that, writes the pin file and sends the changed pins to a running plugin-hostd; the package's upgrade runs it (plugin-qualify#239).

The path unit names the standard folders (/usr/lib/lv2, /usr/lib64/lv2, /usr/local/lib/lv2, /usr/lib/clap, /usr/lib64/clap). The folders the settings file adds (lv2_path, lv2_extra, clap_path, clap_extra) are written into a drop-in of the unit by a systemd generator at boot and at every systemctl daemon-reload, so the file is the one place a machine's extra folders are written.

The path unit watches a folder, not the bundles inside it: a new bundle appearing in a watched folder is seen at once, but a package's own files being replaced in place (an upgrade) is not a change of the folder itself. A packaged plugin is still caught at once, by the distribution's install triggers over the standard folders. An unpackaged bundle replaced in place in an extra folder is caught at the next run of plugin-qualify-sync.timer, at most about 15 minutes after the change.

Keeping the records through an upgrade

An upgrade of plugin-qualify, of the plugins' libraries or of the judge's rules does not call for measuring every plugin again. The figures in the records are carried across and judged again:

plugin-qualify-sync --system --rejudge

--rejudge measures nothing and needs no measuring tool. It reads every record in qualification_dir with the probe output it names, and passes them through the same judge a measurement goes through, under the rules of the running version: a real-time violation under run() or under notes is conditional and pinned isolated, each host's budget is read, and a plugin with no footprint is unknown on a host with a memory budget, never read as fitting. It also judges each record for omx-clap-host, openmixer-console and the Pi boards openmixer-pi-4gb and openmixer-pi-8gb. The verdicts, the tiers and the plugin's pin word are replaced; the figures, the probe output and who took them stay as they were. The record gains a rejudged block with at, by (the version that judged) and figures (tool, measuredAt and runId, as measured). A run that finds nothing to change writes nothing.

A verdict never says more than the figures do. An LV2 plugin's omx-clap-host verdict is decided by its run under the LV2 adapter (the record's adapter block). A record with no measured adapter run reads unknown (qualify.sync.adapter-run-owed), is not offered on the isolated tier, and its pin has no verdict word: plugin-hostd loads such a plugin without grouping it. The same goes for a mod-host or jalv verdict with no run under that host. A record whose plugin's bytes changed, or whose probe output is not the copy it names, is left as it is. Everything left owing is listed under owes in the record and in qualify-owed.json beside the state file (--rejudge prints each line too), with the measurement it needs:

measurement code what pays it
adapter-run qualify.sync.adapter-run-owed --adapter-only, then --rejudge
host-run qualify.sync.host-run-owed a run under that host; today, qualifying the plugin again with --host-profile
qualification qualify.sync.bytes-changed, qualify.sync.figures-unreadable, qualify.sync.no-figures qualifying the plugin again; the next run does so for changed bytes

A probe that crashed took no figures: its record stays unknown with probe.crashed, no pin word and the state's outcome crashed. A crash under a host's run stays unsuitable and refused.

Footprints older records lack are taken apart from everything else:

plugin-qualify-sync --system --memory-only   # the footprints, at the cells a Pi runs
plugin-qualify-sync --system --rejudge       # the verdicts that read them

--memory-only takes the footprint of each plugin the state holds (after instantiate, after activate, at rest, a second instance, and notes held for an instrument) at 48 kHz in blocks of 128 and 256 frames, and nothing else: no sweep, no cost, no latency, no lifecycle, no soak. It goes through the probe runner under the limits of an ordinary run (budget_s, memory_limit), each plugin in processes of its own, an LV2 plugin in a world of its own bundle. An instrument that declares its voice capacity holds that many notes; one that does not holds memory_notes, with basis probe. Only the memory of those cells changes in the record, a cell it lacked joins with no other figure, and a memoryRun block says which runner took them and when. A cell whose run failed holds a reason and no figure. A plugin whose footprints are already merged is skipped, so a pass cut short can be run again; --force takes them again. The pass judges nothing: --rejudge afterwards does.

The adapter runs a record owes are taken apart as well:

plugin-qualify-sync --system --adapter-only  # the runs, at the cells a Pi runs
plugin-qualify-sync --system --rejudge       # the verdicts they decide

--isolated-only runs the isolated step a record still owes: a plugin rated conditional, or one that crashed or hung in the probe, added alone under a plugin-hostd of its own on a private JACK server, with a sine through it for 3 seconds. The record's run keeps its id and gains the step, and the pin follows it; nothing else is measured. A step the machine could not run stays owed.

--adapter-only starts each LV2 plugin the state holds under a fresh omx-clap-host, add then remove through the LV2 adapter, once per cell: 48 kHz in blocks of 128 and 256 frames. Each cell has a private JACK server (jackd -d dummy, so jackd must be installed), so the device's live server is never touched. A command has budget_s seconds, the host's address space is limited as a direct spawn's is, and it is killed with whatever it started. Only the record's adapter block changes: versions (omx-clap-host and plugin-hostd, read from --version), measuredAt, cells, and at its top what the judge reads. A crash or a command that gets no answer in time is the plugin's recorded outcome, at the cell it happened, and reads unsuitable at the next --rejudge. A host that could not be run decides nothing: the block says measured: false, and the run stays owed and is tried again. The pass refuses to start, writing nothing, when a host does not say its version or there is no jackd. A plugin whose block was taken at these host versions is skipped, so a pass cut short can be run again; a host upgrade or --force takes them again. A plugin whose probe failed is skipped: it has no verdict a run could decide.

A leak is not measured. Growth over time takes a soak, which this pass does not run: every record it writes names memoryGrowth under notMeasured, and the last line says leaks not measured.

On a Raspberry Pi 5 a plugin takes under 0.6 s at the median, 5 s at the 90th percentile and 22 s at the 99th; about an hour at most for the 1,542 plugins of the Zynthian set. Those are upper bounds: twice the time the 2026-10-28 records say a whole pass at one cell took, which also ran 30 lifecycles, the sweep, the latency and the cost. A plugin that hangs takes budget_s a cell. The test fixtures take 0.1 s each, both cells, on an x86-64 desktop.

Distributed records

A device that ships with a known plugin set need not measure it again at first start. The qualification records another device of the same machine class wrote for that set are installed read-only, and the sync takes from them every plugin whose files are the bytes that were measured:

/usr/share/omx/qualification/<host class>/<set>/          # system (--system)
$XDG_DATA_HOME/omx/qualification/<host class>/<set>/      # a user run, then each $XDG_DATA_DIRS/omx/qualification

Each <set> directory holds the records (*.qualification.json, each with its probe output *.probe.json) and a provenance.json that says where they come from: the set, the host class, the image, the package versions of the measuring device, the date and the package that installed them. The host class is a directory name: host_class in the settings, or, when it is unset, the board's own name read from the device tree (rpi5 on a Raspberry Pi 5, rpi4 on a Raspberry Pi 4). Where neither gives one, the layer is not read and the run says so.

Before a plugin is measured, the sync looks for a distributed record of it: a CLAP record whose binary is the same .clap path, or an LV2 record of the same plugin uri. The name only finds the record; a record applies when, and only when:

  • every file of its binary.files is installed at that path relative to the plugin's root, with that SHA-256, computed on the device;
  • its schema is the one this version writes and its probe output is one this version's reader accepts, the copy intact (its SHA-256 the one the record names): the same acceptance the sync gives a record of its own, which it never measures again for a newer tool;
  • it holds a verdict for the sync's host_profile, and that verdict ended qualified, refused, crashed or hung. One that could not be measured at the source (unmeasured) is measured here.

A plugin whose distributed records apply is not measured: the records are copied into qualification_dir with the set's provenance object added, its pin is taken from the probe output the record judged, its descriptor is written, and the run says

distributed: http://distrho.sf.net/plugins/3BandEQ: applied (zynthian-vangelis)

A plugin with a distributed record whose files differ is measured as before, and the run says distributed: <uri>: binary differs; one with no distributed record is measured without a word. The summary counts the plugins taken from the layer, distributed N, apart from the ones measured and skipped. A later run treats an applied plugin like one it measured: skipped while its files are unchanged, measured when they change. --force measures everything and reads no distributed record; --no-distributed keeps the layer out of a run.

The package that installs a set is built from a device's qualification_dir by plugin-qualify-records-package:

plugin-qualify-records-package /var/lib/omx/qualification --host-class rpi5 --set zynthian-vangelis \
  --provenance provenance.json --out .

It writes omx-qualification-<host class>-<set>_<version>_all.deb, the version the build date (2026.10.29) unless --version names one. The package installs the records under /usr/share/omx/qualification/<host class>/<set>/ with provenance.json, depends on the plugin-qualify that reads the layer, and is Architecture: all. --provenance names a JSON file (or holds the JSON itself) with what the tool cannot know: the image, the package versions and the source revisions of the device. The tool adds the set, the host class, the package and the date. A record whose probe output is missing or does not match its SHA-256 is left out and named; a record of a plugin that could not be measured (*.unmeasured.json) is left out, since it never applies. The tool builds the Debian package only; an RPM of a set is not built yet.

The container image

podman build -t plugin-qualify -f Containerfile .
podman run --rm -v "$PWD/my-plugins:/plugins:ro" -e LV2_PATH=/plugins -v "$PWD/out:/out" \
  plugin-qualify --host-profile jalv --all --out /out

The image has lilv, the distribution's mod-host and an AddressSanitizer build of mod-host.

Status: the pure steps are in place and tested: target resolution, profile resolution, the verdict, the document and the exit code. The command-line entry point does not yet drive the measuring tools (tools/lv2-measure.mjs, the mod-host sweep). A run that would measure exits 2 and names the missing step, rather than rate a plugin on less than was asked.
